title: Variational Graph Author Topic Modeling

problem.claim: Document topic modeling should provide semantic interpretability while incorporating authorship and publication-venue information.

gap.claim: Most existing VGAE methods lack latent topic structure and semantic interpretability, while most topic models ignore authorship and publication venues.

contributions.claim: A variational graph author topic model integrates semantic interpretability, authorship modeling, and venue modeling within a unified VGAE framework.
A hierarchical multi-layered document graph models authorship and venue information through intra- and cross-layer topic propagation.
Three word relations—contextual, syntactic, and semantic—are modeled as three word sub-layers, and three alternatives for variational divergence are proposed.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that experiments verify the model's effectiveness on supervised and unsupervised tasks.

narrative_sequence.summary: Existing VGAE methods generally lack latent topic structure and semantic interpretability.
Topic structure, authorship, and publication venues are presented as sources of semantic information for documents.
The proposed unified VGAE framework integrates semantic interpretability with authorship and venue modeling.
The method uses a hierarchical multilayer document graph, three word-relation sub-layers, and three variational-divergence alternatives.
Experiments are reported on supervised and unsupervised tasks.

source_observation.claim: Documents are connected through authorship and publication venues, and documents by the same authors are described as tending to reveal similar semantics.

interpretation.claim: Relational metadata can provide useful structure for document topic modeling.

application.claim: When modeling document collections, consider authorship and venue relations as auxiliary graph structure.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish that authorship or venue relations are informative for every corpus or application.

unknowns: Datasets, baselines, metrics, and quantitative results are not specified.
The abstract does not describe the three variational-divergence alternatives in detail.
The abstract does not establish independent verification or reproducibility.
